hook

Every Friday night, millions of families did the same thing. They drove to a bright blue and yellow store, and picked a movie. At its peak, this company had more than nine thousand stores around the world. Then one day, two men walked into its office and offered to sell their tiny company for fifty million dollars. Blockbuster laughed at them. That tiny company was Netflix. This is the story of Blockbuster.
start

Dallas, Texas, nineteen eighty five. A man named David Cook opened a new kind of video store. Most video shops were small, dark and messy. His was huge, bright, and full of thousands of tapes. A computer system tracked every single one. He called it Blockbuster Video.
growth

A businessman named Wayne Huizenga saw the future, and bought in. He opened stores at a crazy speed. At one point, a new Blockbuster opened somewhere about every seventeen hours. In nineteen ninety four, the media giant Viacom bought the company for more than eight billion dollars.
friday

Blockbuster became a ritual. Walking the aisles. Grabbing popcorn and candy at the counter. Hoping the new release wasn't all gone. Every tape had a sticker that said, be kind, rewind. And if you brought it back late, you paid. Late fees made Blockbuster hundreds of millions of dollars a year.
netflix

Those late fees made a lot of people angry. One of them was Reed Hastings. Legend says he got a forty dollar late fee for a movie he forgot to return. In nineteen ninety seven, he and Marc Randolph started Netflix. You chose movies on a website, and the DVDs arrived in the mail, in a little red envelope. And there were no late fees.
offer

In two thousand, Netflix was losing money. So Hastings and Randolph flew to Dallas, to meet Blockbuster's boss, John Antioco. Their offer? Buy Netflix for fifty million dollars, and we'll run your online business. Randolph later said the Blockbuster team could barely stop themselves from laughing. The answer was no.
peak

And why would they say yes? In two thousand four, Blockbuster was at its peak. More than nine thousand stores. About eighty four thousand employees. Billions of dollars every year. Netflix was a tiny company selling DVDs in envelopes.
fight

But Antioco saw the danger. He launched Blockbuster Online, and he even got rid of late fees. It was working. But it cost a fortune, and the investors were furious. Antioco was pushed out. The new boss went back to the stores. He even said Netflix was not on the radar screen.
stream

Then the world changed. Red kiosks rented DVDs for one dollar a night. And in two thousand seven, Netflix started streaming. No store. No envelope. No waiting. Just press play. Families stopped driving to Blockbuster. The aisles went quiet.
fall

Blockbuster was drowning in debt. In September twenty ten, the company filed for bankruptcy. Stores closed one after another, across the whole world. Thousands of people lost their jobs. By twenty fourteen, almost every Blockbuster on Earth had shut its doors.
end

Except one. In the small town of Bend, Oregon, the last Blockbuster on the planet is still open, and people travel from all over the world just to visit it. And Netflix, the company Blockbuster could have bought for fifty million dollars, is now worth hundreds of billions. Sometimes the biggest mistake is laughing at the little guy.
